messages.subject: installing rstan
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to install rstan on my mac using R version 2.15.1, following the instructions here. I've got the Rcpp, RcppEigen, and inline packages installed.  Now, when I try to run

> install.packages('rstan', type = 'source')

I get compilation errors that I'm having trouble resolving. I've pasted all of the output at the end of this message, but it's basically several errors that look like

../inst/include/stansrc/stan/math/boost_error_handling.hpp:430: error: ISO C++ does not support ‘long long’

Does anyone have any suggestions for how I can resolve this? My apologies if I've missed one of the instructions for setting my machine up or something like that.

Thanks in advance,

Dennis

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] installing rstan
parts:
Thanks for the report and sorry you hit a snag.

We're a bit puzzled by this error as nobody else
has had it on the Mac. We're going to do a patch
release next week and I think we can get rid of
the "long long" types altogether.

Which version of g++ are you using? You can pull
up a terminal and type "g++ --version" to tell.

Also, which version of Mac OS X?

- Bob

I would guess that you have a Makevars file in your home directory, like

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:~/.R$ ls
Makevars

that specifies -pedantic. Or maybe somewhere in the Makeconf file, which can be found by executing in R

file.path(R.home(component = 'etc'), .Platform$r_arch, 'Makeconf')

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: installing rstan

Hi,

Thanks! I'm using Rcpp for another project, and had indeed created a
Makevars file which was in the location Ben suggested. I took away the
-pedantic flag and the package installed fine.

(Bob, I think that was the issue, but in case it's still useful, I
have OS X 10.7.4 and g++ version 4.2.1.)

Thanks for your help!

d

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: installing rstan
parts:
On 9/21/12 7:00 PM, Dennis Feehan wrote:
> Hi,
>
> Thanks! I'm using Rcpp for another project, and had indeed created a
> Makevars file which was in the location Ben suggested. I took away the
> -pedantic flag and the package installed fine.
Thanks for letting us know that fixed the issue.

> (Bob, I think that was the issue, but in case it's still useful, I
> have OS X 10.7.4 and g++ version 4.2.1.)

Nope -- I don't need the OS report any more.

Your report was helpful in that it made us realize
we'd reintroduced a couple of long-long instances
in error-handling and I/O code. (We have to remember
to ONLY cover the pre-C++-11 primitive types!).

We originally ran into the long-long issue with Rcpp,
which is set to be CRAN compatible by default. CRAN
is, perhaps not surprisingly, set to use -pedantic mode
for packages.

- Bob
